title: Paediatric Early Warning Score (PEWS)
purpose: Bedside aggregate score for early recognition of clinical deterioration in paediatric inpatients. Drives nursing-led escalation pathways.

population.notes: Children up to 16 years. Age-band specific vital-sign thresholds required (use APLS / RCPCH age bands).

items.label: Behaviour: 0 = playing/appropriate; 1 = sleeping; 2 = irritable; 3 = lethargic/confused or reduced response to pain
Cardiovascular: 0 = pink or CRT 1–2 s; 1 = pale or CRT 3 s; 2 = grey or CRT 4 s, tachycardia 20 above normal; 3 = grey + mottled or CRT ≥5 s, tachycardia 30 above normal or bradycardia

Respiratory: 0 = within normal range, no recession; 1 = rate >10 above normal, using accessory muscles, FiO₂ 30% or 3 L/min; 2 = rate >20 above normal, recessions, FiO₂ 40% or 6 L/min; 3 = rate ≥5 below normal with sternal recession/grunting, FiO₂ ≥50% or 8 L/min

scoring.notes: Add 2 if quarter-hourly nebulisers; add 2 for persistent vomiting post-surgery. Age-band vital-sign normals must be applied; do not use adult ranges. Many UK trusts use a modified PEWS (Bedside PEWS) with additional parameters (SpO₂, blood pressure, capillary refill discrete points).

interpretation.action: Inform nurse-in-charge; increase observation frequency to hourly. Consider medical review.
Senior nurse + medical team review; reassess airway, breathing, circulation. Escalate to registrar.
Immediate medical team / outreach activation. Consider PICU referral. ABC priorities.

caution: Single-point PEWS scores miss the patient who is critically ill but does not breach a band (e.g. compensated shock with normal HR). Use trend, parental concern, and clinical gestalt alongside the score. ALWAYS apply age-band vital-sign normals (RCPCH).

references.label: RCPCH National PEWS Implementation Programme.
Parshuram CS et al. Effect of a paediatric early warning system on all-cause mortality in hospitalised paediatric patients (EPOCH cluster RCT). JAMA 2018.

title: Paediatric Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (pSOFA)
purpose: Organ-dysfunction score for children, adapted from adult SOFA — used to identify and risk-stratify paediatric sepsis (Phoenix Sepsis Criteria 2024 are now preferred for definition; pSOFA remains widely used for severity).

population.notes: Birth to 18 years. Use age-adjusted MAP and creatinine cut-offs (see Matics & Sanchez-Pinto 2017).

items.label: Respiration (PaO₂/FiO₂ or SpO₂/FiO₂): 0 = ≥400/≥292; 1 = 300–399/264–291; 2 = 200–299/221–263; 3 = 100–199 with ventilation/148–220; 4 = <100 with ventilation/<148

Cardiovascular (age-adjusted MAP or vasopressor): 0 = no hypotension; 1 = MAP < age cut-off; 2 = dopamine ≤5 or dobutamine any; 3 = dopamine >5 or adrenaline/noradrenaline ≤0.1; 4 = dopamine >15 or adrenaline/noradrenaline >0.1 µg/kg/min
Renal (creatinine, age-adjusted µmol/L): 0 = <age cut-off; 1–4 = increasing categories per Matics & Sanchez-Pinto table

scoring.notes: Sum of 6 organ-system sub-scores (0–4 each). Calculated daily during ICU admission. Age-adjusted MAP and creatinine cut-offs are essential — see source paper.

interpretation.meaning: Sepsis-3 paediatric adaptation (Schlapbach 2018; superseded by Phoenix 2024)
interpretation.action: Initiate sepsis bundle. Consider source identification, empiric antimicrobials, fluid resuscitation per local protocol.

caution: Phoenix Sepsis Criteria (Schlapbach JAMA 2024) replaced the SIRS / paediatric Sepsis-3 / pSOFA framework as the consensus paediatric sepsis definition. pSOFA remains useful for ICU organ-dysfunction tracking; do not use it as the sole sepsis-screening tool in 2024+ — see Phoenix instead.

references.label: Matics TJ, Sanchez-Pinto LN. Adaptation and validation of a pediatric sequential organ failure assessment score and evaluation of the Sepsis-3 definitions in critically ill children. JAMA Pediatrics 2017;171:e172352.
Schlapbach LJ et al. International consensus criteria for pediatric sepsis and septic shock (Phoenix). JAMA 2024;331:665-674.

title: ASCVD 10-year risk (Pooled Cohort Equations)
purpose: Estimate 10-year risk of first atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease event (non-fatal MI, CHD death, fatal or non-fatal stroke) in primary prevention. Drives statin initiation decisions per ACC/AHA.

population.notes: Adults 40–79 years without clinical ASCVD or LDL ≥190 mg/dL (4.9 mmol/L). Validated in non-Hispanic White and African-American populations; calibration in other groups variable.

scoring.notes: Sex- and race-specific regression equations from Goff DC et al. 2014 (Circulation 129:S49-73). Cannot be reproduced by manual summation — use the ACC/AHA risk calculator (https://tools.acc.org/ascvd-risk-estimator-plus) or any validated implementation. The PREVENT equations (AHA 2023, Khan SS et al. Circulation) are the modern successor — estimate 10y/30y total CVD risk in adults 30–79; do not require race; include kidney function and metabolic factors.

interpretation.action: Risk discussion; consider risk enhancers (family history premature CVD, CKD, inflammatory disease, South Asian ancestry, LDL ≥160). Consider CAC scoring if uncertain.
Moderate-intensity statin recommended after shared decision-making. CAC scoring may reclassify.

caution: Overestimates risk in some contemporary cohorts. Avoid sole reliance — incorporate risk enhancers and shared decision-making. PREVENT equations are increasingly preferred for new patients.

references.label: Goff DC Jr et al. 2013 ACC/AHA Guideline on the Assessment of Cardiovascular Risk. Circulation 2014;129:S49-S73.
Khan SS et al. Novel Prediction Equations for Absolute Risk Assessment of Total Cardiovascular Disease (PREVENT). Circulation 2023.

title: APACHE II
purpose: Assess severity of illness and predict ICU mortality. Calculated within the first 24 h of ICU admission.

population.notes: Adults in ICU within first 24 h of admission. Not validated for paediatrics; use PRISM / PIM for children.

items.label: Acute physiology score: temperature, MAP, heart rate, respiratory rate, FiO₂-adjusted oxygenation, arterial pH, sodium, potassium, creatinine (×2 if AKI), haematocrit, WBC, GCS (15 − actual) — each 0–4 points
Chronic health: severe organ failure / immunocompromise = 5 if emergency surgery or non-operative; = 2 if elective postoperative

scoring.notes: Sum APS + age + chronic health points. Look up predicted mortality via the disease-specific table (Knaus 1985). Modern ICUs use APACHE IV or SAPS 3 (better calibration); APACHE II remains widely cited and used for case-mix adjustment.

interpretation.action: Consider goals-of-care discussion alongside aggressive treatment.
Goals-of-care discussion with family; consider limits of escalation.

caution: Risk prediction is for COHORTS, not individuals — do not withdraw care on the basis of an APACHE score for any single patient. Modern calibration is poor in some populations; consider APACHE IV / SAPS 3 / MPM if available.

references.label: Knaus WA et al. APACHE II: a severity of disease classification system. Crit Care Med 1985;13:818-29.

title: Systemic Inflammatory Response Syndrome (SIRS)
purpose: Historical sepsis-screening criteria. Now SUPERSEDED by qSOFA / Sepsis-3 for sepsis definition, but still widely used for ICU screening and present in many EHR alerts.

population.notes: Adults. Not for paediatric sepsis screening — use Phoenix Sepsis Criteria 2024.

items.label: Respiratory rate > 20/min or PaCO₂ < 32 mmHg (4.3 kPa)

scoring.notes: ≥ 2 met = SIRS positive. Sepsis (old Sepsis-1 definition) = SIRS + suspected infection.

interpretation.action: Sepsis less likely; continue clinical assessment.

If infection suspected, evaluate as possible sepsis: send cultures, lactate, full sepsis bundle; do NOT delay antibiotics for definitive imaging. Use qSOFA / NEWS2 for severity grading per Sepsis-3 / Surviving Sepsis Campaign.

caution: Sepsis-3 (2016) replaced SIRS with qSOFA + clinical suspicion. SIRS lacks specificity (very high false-positive rate — pneumonia, dehydration, post-op patients all trigger). Use as a TRIGGER for further evaluation, not as a sepsis diagnosis.

references.label: Bone RC et al. Definitions for sepsis and organ failure. Chest 1992;101:1644-55.
Singer M et al. The Third International Consensus Definitions for Sepsis and Septic Shock (Sepsis-3). JAMA 2016;315:801-10.

title: National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS)
purpose: Quantify stroke severity at presentation; drives thrombolysis / thrombectomy decisions and monitors clinical evolution.

population.notes: Adults with suspected acute ischaemic stroke. Requires certified training for inter-rater reliability.

items.label: 1b. LOC questions (month, age): 0 both correct → 2 neither correct
1c. LOC commands (open/close eyes, grip): 0 both → 2 neither
5a. Motor arm — left (0 no drift → 4 no movement; 9 amputation/joint fusion)
6a. Motor leg — left (0 no drift → 4 no movement)
7. Limb ataxia (0 absent → 2 in two limbs; 9 amputation)
9. Best language (0 normal → 3 mute, global aphasia)

scoring.notes: Items scored 9 (amputation, intubated, etc.) are EXCLUDED from total (not zeroed). Reassess every 15 min during thrombolysis, hourly first 6 h, then per local pathway.

interpretation.action: Continue investigation if clinical suspicion remains.
Consider thrombolysis on individual basis (debate around minor non-disabling stroke; ENCHANTED-2 / PRISMS studies).
Thrombolysis if within window and no contraindication. Consider mechanical thrombectomy if proximal large-vessel occlusion.
Mechanical thrombectomy assessment; aggressive medical optimisation; ICU.

caution: Heavily weighted to dominant-hemisphere cortical signs — a posterior circulation stroke or right-hemisphere lesion can be devastating with a low NIHSS. Do NOT use NIHSS alone to deny thrombolysis. Posterior circulation imaging threshold should be low.

references.label: Brott T et al. Measurements of acute cerebral infarction: a clinical examination scale. Stroke 1989;20:864-70.

Burden of illness — moderate symptoms (intermediate; choose ONE of mild/moderate/severe burden)
No COPD (active emphysema, chronic bronchitis, oxygen therapy)
Solid tumour, or haematologic malignancy with no previous fungal infection
Outpatient status at onset of fever

scoring.notes: Burden of illness: pick ONE of mild (5) / moderate (3) / severe (0).

interpretation.action: Consider oral antibiotics (e.g. amoxicillin-clavulanate + ciprofloxacin) and outpatient management with daily review and 24/7 access to care, provided no clinical instability.
Admit; empirical broad-spectrum IV antibiotics within 1 h (anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam ± vancomycin if indicated); evaluate source.

caution: Local MDR resistance patterns and patient-specific risk factors override the score. Discuss outpatient management with the patient's oncology team before discharge.

references.label: Klastersky J et al. The Multinational Association for Supportive Care in Cancer risk index. JCO 2000;18:3038-51.
IDSA Guideline: Clinical Practice Guideline for the Use of Antimicrobial Agents in Neutropenic Patients with Cancer. CID 2011.

title: TIMI Risk Score for STEMI
purpose: Predict 30-day mortality in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction receiving fibrinolysis.

population.notes: Adults with STEMI eligible for fibrinolytic therapy. Derived from InTIME-II.

scoring.notes: Age contributes either 2 (65–74) or 3 (≥75), not both.

interpretation.action: Consider rescue PCI; aggressive monitoring; cardiogenic shock pathway readiness.

caution: Derived for fibrinolysis-treated STEMI. Not validated as a primary triage tool for primary PCI.

references.label: Morrow DA et al. TIMI risk score for ST-elevation MI. Circulation 2000;102:2031-7.

title: TIMI Risk Index
purpose: Simple bedside index for 30-day mortality risk after STEMI using only age, heart rate and systolic BP.

scoring.notes: TRI = HR × (age/10)² / SBP. See Wiviott SD et al. JAMA 2001;286:1356-9 for risk strata table.

references.label: Wiviott SD et al. Application of the TIMI Risk Index. JAMA 2001;286:1356-9.

title: GRACE 2.0 ACS risk score
purpose: Estimate in-hospital and 6-month mortality in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome.

population.notes: Adults with NSTEMI, STEMI or unstable angina. Used to triage to early invasive vs conservative strategy in NSTE-ACS.

items.label: Variables: age, heart rate, systolic BP, serum creatinine, Killip class, cardiac arrest at admission, ST-segment deviation, elevated cardiac biomarkers

scoring.notes: Non-linear regression with continuous variables. Use the official GRACE 2.0 calculator (https://www.outcomes-umassmed.org/grace) — point-wise estimation is no longer recommended.

interpretation.action: Early (within 72 h) invasive strategy in NSTE-ACS per ESC.
Early (< 24 h) invasive strategy per ESC.

references.label: Fox KAA et al. GRACE 2.0 ACS risk calculator. BMJ Open 2014;4:e004425.
ESC 2023 Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes.

title: EuroSCORE II
purpose: Predict in-hospital mortality after adult cardiac surgery.

items.label: 18 logistic regression variables: age, sex, renal function (CrCl), extracardiac arteriopathy, poor mobility, prior cardiac surgery, chronic lung disease, active endocarditis, critical preoperative state, diabetes on insulin, NYHA class, CCS angina, LV function, recent MI, pulmonary hypertension, urgency, weight of intervention, surgery on thoracic aorta

scoring.notes: Logistic regression. Use the official EuroSCORE II calculator (https://www.euroscore.org/calc.html). Replaces original additive/logistic EuroSCORE.

interpretation.band: Result is a predicted in-hospital mortality percentage
interpretation.meaning: Use for shared decision-making and benchmarking, not single-patient gating.

caution: Calibration drifts over time and across regions; recalibration to local cohort is recommended for institutional benchmarking.

references.label: Nashef SA et al. EuroSCORE II. Eur J Cardiothorac Surg 2012;41:734-44.

title: STS Adult Cardiac Surgery Risk Score
purpose: Predict operative mortality and major morbidity after adult cardiac surgery (CABG, valve, combined).

items.label: Procedure-specific multivariable models using demographics, comorbidities, prior cardiovascular events, haemodynamics and procedural urgency

scoring.notes: Use the official online STS calculator (https://www.sts.org/resources/risk-calculator). Coefficients are recalibrated periodically against the STS National Database.

interpretation.action: Heart team discussion; consider TAVI / transcatheter approaches.

references.label: Society of Thoracic Surgeons Adult Cardiac Surgery Risk Models; periodic recalibration.

title: DAPT Score
purpose: Decide whether to extend dual antiplatelet therapy beyond 12 months after PCI by balancing ischaemic vs bleeding risk.

interpretation.action: Consider stopping P2Y12 inhibitor at 12 months.

references.label: Yeh RW et al. Development and Validation of a Prediction Rule for Benefit and Harm of Dual Antiplatelet Therapy Beyond 1 Year After PCI. JAMA 2016;315:1735-49.

title: PRECISE-DAPT Score
purpose: Predict out-of-hospital major bleeding on DAPT after PCI; guide DAPT duration.

scoring.notes: Continuous variables in a nomogram (0–100). Use the published nomogram / online calculator.

interpretation.action: Standard or longer DAPT durations are reasonable.

references.label: Costa F et al. PRECISE-DAPT score. Lancet 2017;389:1025-34.

title: CRUSADE Bleeding Score
purpose: Estimate in-hospital major bleeding risk in patients with NSTEMI receiving antithrombotic therapy.

scoring.notes: Each variable contributes weighted points per the published nomogram; use the official CRUSADE calculator.

interpretation.action: Consider radial access, reduce/avoid GP IIb/IIIa, weight- and renal-adjust anticoagulants.

references.label: Subherwal S et al. CRUSADE bleeding score. Circulation 2009;119:1873-82.

title: ATRIA Stroke Risk Score (AF)
purpose: Alternative to CHA2DS2-VASc for ischaemic-stroke risk in atrial fibrillation.

items.label: Prior stroke present — age points are doubled per ATRIA matrix (max 9)

scoring.notes: Prior stroke modifies the age sub-score (use the published two-column lookup).

references.label: Singer DE et al. ATRIA stroke risk score. J Am Heart Assoc 2013;2:e000250.

title: ATRIA Bleeding Risk Score
purpose: Estimate major bleeding risk on warfarin in atrial fibrillation; alternative to HAS-BLED.

interpretation.action: Address modifiable factors; do not withhold anticoagulation on this score alone.

references.label: Fang MC et al. ATRIA bleeding risk score. JACC 2011;58:395-401.

title: ORBIT Bleeding Risk Score
purpose: Predict major bleeding in AF patients on anticoagulation; alternative to HAS-BLED and ATRIA-Bleed.

references.label: O'Brien EC et al. ORBIT bleeding risk score. Eur Heart J 2015;36:3258-64.

title: ABC Stroke Risk Score (AF)
purpose: Biomarker-based stroke risk in atrial fibrillation (Age, Biomarkers, Clinical history).

scoring.notes: Use published nomogram / online calculator. Continuous variables; pointwise summation invalid.

interpretation.meaning: Use threshold per local guideline (typically 1%/yr to favour anticoagulation).

references.label: Hijazi Z et al. ABC stroke risk score. Eur Heart J 2016;37:1582-90.

title: ABC Bleeding Risk Score (AF)
purpose: Biomarker-based bleeding risk in atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation.

items.label: Biomarkers: haemoglobin, hs-cTnT, GDF-15 (or cystatin C / creatinine clearance)

scoring.notes: Nomogram / online calculator.

interpretation.meaning: Use alongside stroke risk for net benefit assessment.

references.label: Hijazi Z et al. ABC bleeding risk score. Lancet 2016;387:2302-11.

title: GWTG-HF Risk Score
purpose: Predict in-hospital mortality in patients admitted with acute decompensated heart failure.

scoring.notes: Use the published GWTG-HF point lookup or AHA online calculator.

interpretation.action: Senior input; consider ICU / advanced HF therapies.

references.label: Peterson PN et al. GWTG-HF risk score. Circ Cardiovasc Qual Outcomes 2010;3:25-32.

title: Killip Classification (acute MI)
purpose: Bedside clinical classification of heart failure severity in acute MI; prognostic.

items.label: Class I — no clinical signs of heart failure
Class II — rales / crackles, S3, raised JVP
Class IV — cardiogenic shock (SBP < 90, evidence of hypoperfusion)

scoring.notes: Patient is assigned to ONE class based on examination.

interpretation.action: Cardiogenic shock pathway; vasopressors, urgent revascularisation, consider mechanical support.

references.label: Killip T, Kimball JT. Treatment of myocardial infarction in a coronary care unit. Am J Cardiol 1967;20:457-64.

title: Forrester Classification (acute MI)
purpose: Haemodynamic classification of acute MI by cardiac index and pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.

scoring.notes: Requires invasive haemodynamic monitoring or echocardiographic surrogates.

references.label: Forrester JS et al. Medical therapy of acute myocardial infarction. NEJM 1976;295:1356-62.

title: Pulmonary Embolism Severity Index (full)
purpose: Predict 30-day mortality in acute pulmonary embolism to guide site of care.

scoring.notes: Age in years is added directly to the categorical points.

interpretation.action: Outpatient treatment may be appropriate if no other concerns.
Admit; consider thrombolysis if haemodynamically unstable.

references.label: Aujesky D et al. Derivation and validation of the PESI. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2005;172:1041-6.

title: Hestia Criteria for Outpatient PE Management
purpose: Identify acute PE patients suitable for outpatient management.

items.label: Haemodynamically unstable (SBP < 100, HR > 100 + signs of poor perfusion)
Active bleeding or high bleeding risk
> 24 h oxygen required to maintain SaO₂ > 90%
Severe pain needing IV analgesia > 24 h
Medical or social reason for admission > 24 h

scoring.notes: ANY criterion present = NOT eligible for outpatient management.

interpretation.action: Discharge on anticoagulation with early review.

references.label: Zondag W et al. Hestia criteria. J Thromb Haemost 2011;9:1500-7.

title: WHO Functional Class — Pulmonary Hypertension
purpose: Functional classification of symptom severity in pulmonary hypertension; drives therapy escalation.

items.label: Class I — no limitation of ordinary physical activity
Class II — slight limitation; comfortable at rest
Class III — marked limitation; less-than-ordinary activity causes symptoms
Class IV — unable to perform any activity; symptoms at rest

interpretation.action: Consider mono- or dual oral therapy per ESC/ERS.
Combination oral ± parenteral prostacyclin; transplant referral.

references.label: ESC/ERS 2022 Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension.

title: Revised Ghent Criteria for Marfan Syndrome
purpose: Diagnostic criteria for Marfan syndrome integrating systemic features, aortic root dilatation, ectopia lentis and FBN1 mutation.

population.notes: Patients with suspected Marfan syndrome. Different rules apply with vs without family history.

items.label: Ectopia lentis + FBN1 mutation known to cause aortic disease
Positive family history + ectopia lentis OR systemic score ≥ 7 OR aortic Z ≥ 2 (adult) / ≥ 3 (under 20)

scoring.notes: Systemic score: wrist + thumb sign (3), pectus carinatum (2), hindfoot deformity (2), pneumothorax (2), dural ectasia (2), protrusio acetabuli (2), reduced US:LS and increased arm/height (1), scoliosis (1), reduced elbow extension (1), 3 of 5 facial features (1), skin striae (1), myopia >3 D (1), MV prolapse (1). Maximum 20.

interpretation.action: Genetics referral; cardiology surveillance; family screening.

references.label: Loeys BL et al. Revised Ghent nosology for Marfan syndrome. J Med Genet 2010;47:476-85.

title: Modified Sgarbossa Criteria (LBBB / paced rhythm)
purpose: Identify acute MI in the presence of LBBB or ventricular paced rhythm.

items.label: Concordant ST elevation ≥ 1 mm in any lead
Concordant ST depression ≥ 1 mm in V1–V3
Discordant ST elevation with ST/S ratio ≤ −0.25 in any lead

scoring.notes: ANY criterion positive = highly specific for acute MI.

references.label: Smith SW et al. Modified Sgarbossa. Ann Emerg Med 2012;60:766-76.

title: Inotrope / Vasoactive-Inotropic Score (VIS)
purpose: Quantify pharmacological cardiovascular support intensity, particularly in post-cardiac-surgery and paediatric ICU.

scoring.notes: VIS = dopamine + dobutamine + 100×(adrenaline + noradrenaline) + 10×milrinone + 10000×vasopressin (all in µg/kg/min where applicable).

interpretation.action: Re-evaluate haemodynamic strategy; consider mechanical support.

references.label: Gaies MG et al. Vasoactive-inotropic score. Pediatr Crit Care Med 2010;11:234-8.

title: 6-Minute Walk Test (6MWT)
purpose: Submaximal exercise test of functional capacity; widely used in heart failure, COPD and pulmonary hypertension.

items.label: Distance walked in 6 minutes on a flat 30 m course (metres)

scoring.notes: Compare against age/sex predicted values (Enright reference equations). Minimal clinically important difference ~30 m.

interpretation.action: Associated with high mortality in HF / PH.

references.label: ATS Statement: Guidelines for the Six-Minute Walk Test. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2002;166:111-7.

title: Seattle Heart Failure Model
purpose: Estimate 1-, 2- and 5-year survival in patients with chronic heart failure.

items.label: Demographics, NYHA class, ischaemic aetiology, LVEF, systolic BP, medications (ACEi/ARB/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, diuretic doses, statin, allopurinol, ICD, CRT), labs (sodium, haemoglobin, lymphocyte %, uric acid, cholesterol)

scoring.notes: Multivariable Cox regression. Use the official online SHFM calculator (https://depts.washington.edu/shfm).

interpretation.band: Result is 1/2/5-year survival probability and mean life expectancy
interpretation.meaning: Use for shared decision-making, transplant / LVAD listing discussions.

caution: Calibration varies post-ARNI era; many newer therapies (SGLT2, vericiguat, omecamtiv) are not in the original model.

references.label: Levy WC et al. The Seattle Heart Failure Model. Circulation 2006;113:1424-33.

title: MAGGIC Heart Failure Risk Score
purpose: Predict 1- and 3-year mortality in chronic heart failure (preserved or reduced EF).

items.label: Age, LVEF, NYHA class, sex, BMI, systolic BP, creatinine, diabetes, COPD, current smoker, HF duration, beta-blocker, ACE/ARB

scoring.notes: Meta-analytic regression from 30 cohorts. Online calculator at https://www.heartfailurerisk.org/.

interpretation.meaning: Use to stratify; combine with clinical judgement and biomarkers (NT-proBNP).

references.label: Pocock SJ et al. MAGGIC HF risk score. Eur Heart J 2013;34:1404-13.

title: NT-proBNP Diagnostic Cut-offs for Heart Failure
purpose: Age-adjusted NT-proBNP thresholds to rule in / rule out heart failure in acute and ambulatory settings.

scoring.notes: Cut-offs are diagnostic thresholds, not a score; values in pg/mL.

references.label: ESC 2021 Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of acute and chronic heart failure.
Januzzi JL et al. ICON-RELOADED. JACC 2018;71:1191-200.

title: Hematopoietic Cell Transplantation–Comorbidity Index
purpose: Predict non-relapse mortality after allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation.

references.label: Sorror ML et al. HCT-CI. Blood 2005;106:2912-9.

title: NEXUS Criteria for C-spine Imaging
purpose: Identify low-risk blunt trauma patients in whom cervical spine imaging can be safely omitted.

scoring.notes: ALL 5 must be met to defer imaging.

interpretation.meaning: Very low probability of clinically significant C-spine injury

interpretation.action: C-spine imaging (CT preferred in higher-risk trauma).

references.label: Hoffman JR et al. Validity of NEXUS criteria. NEJM 2000;343:94-9.

title: Canadian C-Spine Rule
purpose: Decide whether cervical spine imaging is required after blunt trauma in alert, stable adults.

population.notes: Alert (GCS 15), stable, blunt trauma, age ≥ 16. Not for non-trauma neck pain or penetrating trauma.

items.label: High-risk factor present (age ≥ 65, dangerous mechanism, paraesthesia in extremities)
Low-risk factor allowing safe ROM assessment (simple rear-end MVC, sitting in ED, ambulatory, delayed onset neck pain, no midline tenderness)
Able to actively rotate neck 45° left and right

scoring.notes: Algorithm: (1) any high-risk factor → image; (2) if none, any low-risk factor allows safe ROM testing; (3) if able to rotate 45° both ways → no imaging.

interpretation.meaning: High-risk feature or unable to rotate
Low-risk factor present + able to rotate

references.label: Stiell IG et al. Canadian C-Spine Rule. NEJM 2003;349:2510-8.

title: Canadian CT Head Rule
purpose: Identify minor head-injured adults who need CT scanning.

population.notes: Adults ≥ 16, GCS 13–15 after blunt head trauma with witnessed LOC, amnesia or confusion. Excludes anticoagulated patients, seizure, age < 16.

items.label: High risk — GCS < 15 at 2 h post-injury
High risk — suspected open or depressed skull fracture
High risk — any sign of basal skull fracture
Medium risk — amnesia before impact > 30 min

scoring.notes: High-risk criteria identify patients needing neurosurgical intervention; medium-risk criteria identify any clinically important brain injury.

interpretation.meaning: CT for clinically important brain injury

references.label: Stiell IG et al. Canadian CT Head Rule. Lancet 2001;357:1391-6.

title: New Orleans Criteria (head injury)
purpose: Identify minor head-injured patients with GCS 15 and LOC who need CT.

population.notes: Adults with minor blunt head trauma, GCS 15, witnessed LOC.

scoring.notes: ANY criterion positive → CT head.

references.label: Haydel MJ et al. NOC for CT in minor head injury. NEJM 2000;343:100-5.

title: PECARN Paediatric Head Injury (< 2 yr)
purpose: Identify children under 2 with minor head trauma at very low risk of clinically important traumatic brain injury (ciTBI).

population.notes: Children < 2 yr, GCS ≥ 14, minor blunt head trauma.

items.label: AMS (agitation, somnolence, repetitive questioning, slow response) or GCS ≤ 14

scoring.notes: Stepwise rule. Presence of AMS or palpable skull fracture → CT recommended. Other features → observation vs CT based on clinical judgment / multiple findings.

interpretation.action: Observation or CT per shared decision-making.

references.label: Kuppermann N et al. PECARN head injury rule. Lancet 2009;374:1160-70.

title: PECARN Paediatric Head Injury (≥ 2 yr)
purpose: Identify children 2 yr and older with minor head trauma at very low risk of ciTBI.

scoring.notes: Stepwise rule. AMS or basilar skull fracture → CT recommended.

interpretation.action: Observation or CT per shared decision.

references.label: Kuppermann N et al. PECARN head injury rule. Lancet 2009;374:1160-70.

title: PECARN Paediatric Cervical Spine Injury
purpose: Risk-stratify children with blunt trauma for cervical spine injury.

items.label: Altered mental status (GCS < 15 or AVPU < A)
Conditions predisposing to CSI (e.g. Down syndrome, Klippel-Feil)

scoring.notes: Derivation study (Leonard 2011); presence of ≥ 1 factor increases risk and supports imaging.

references.label: Leonard JC et al. PECARN cervical-spine factors. Ann Emerg Med 2011;58:145-55.

title: ROSIER Scale (Recognition of Stroke in ER)
purpose: Bedside differentiation of acute stroke from stroke mimics in the emergency department.

interpretation.action: Reassess for mimics; do not delay imaging if clinical suspicion remains.

references.label: Nor AM et al. ROSIER scale. Lancet Neurol 2005;4:727-34.

title: Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale
purpose: Three-item screening tool for prehospital identification of stroke.

scoring.notes: Any one positive item raises stroke probability sharply.

interpretation.action: Activate prehospital stroke pathway; rapid transport to stroke centre.

references.label: Kothari RU et al. Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale. Ann Emerg Med 1999;33:373-8.

title: Los Angeles Motor Scale
purpose: Prehospital severity scale to identify large-vessel occlusion (LVO) stroke.

items.label: Arm drift — absent (0) / drifts down (1) / falls rapidly (2)
Grip strength — normal (0) / weak grip (1) / no grip (2)

references.label: Llanes JN et al. LAMS. Prehosp Emerg Care 2004;8:46-50.

title: RACE Scale
purpose: Prehospital scale to identify LVO stroke (Rapid Arterial oCclusion Evaluation).

items.label: Arm motor function — normal (0) / mild paresis (1) / severe (2)
Leg motor function — normal (0) / mild (1) / severe (2)
Aphasia (if R-hemiparesis): perform commands — performs both (0) / one (1) / neither (2); OR Agnosia (if L-hemiparesis): recognises arm and impairment — both (0) / one (1) / neither (2)

references.label: Pérez de la Ossa N et al. RACE scale. Stroke 2014;45:87-91.

title: ABCD2-I (TIA with imaging)
purpose: Refine 7-day stroke risk after TIA by adding DWI and large-artery imaging to the ABCD2 score.

items.label: Clinical: unilateral weakness (2) / speech without weakness (1)
Ipsilateral ≥ 50% large-artery stenosis or intracranial stenosis

interpretation.action: Admit; expedited workup; dual antiplatelet ± anticoagulation per aetiology.

references.label: Giles MF et al. ABCD2-I. Stroke 2010;41:1907-13.

title: HEMORR2HAGES Bleeding Score
purpose: Estimate annual major bleeding risk in older adults with AF on warfarin.

references.label: Gage BF et al. HEMORR2HAGES. Am Heart J 2006;151:713-9.

title: Revised Trauma Score
purpose: Physiological trauma severity score for triage and outcome prediction.

scoring.notes: RTS = 0.9368·GCS_c + 0.7326·SBP_c + 0.2908·RR_c. Triage RTS (T-RTS) = simple sum of coded values (0–12).

references.label: Champion HR et al. A revision of the Trauma Score. J Trauma 1989;29:623-9.

title: Injury Severity Score
purpose: Anatomical scoring system for multi-system trauma; predicts mortality.

items.label: Sum of squares of the three highest AIS (Abbreviated Injury Scale) scores across the six body regions

scoring.notes: ISS = AIS1² + AIS2² + AIS3². Any AIS = 6 (unsurvivable) sets ISS = 75 automatically.

references.label: Baker SP et al. The Injury Severity Score. J Trauma 1974;14:187-96.

title: Shock Index
purpose: Bedside marker of haemodynamic instability; predicts need for massive transfusion and mortality in trauma, sepsis and post-partum haemorrhage.

scoring.notes: SI = HR / SBP. Modified SI = HR / MAP.

interpretation.action: Active resuscitation; activate transfusion / sepsis protocols.

references.label: Allgöwer M, Buri C. Schockindex. Dtsch Med Wochenschr 1967;92:1947-50.

title: MGAP Score (trauma)
purpose: Predict in-hospital mortality in trauma using mechanism, GCS, age and systolic BP.

references.label: Sartorius D et al. MGAP score. J Trauma 2010;69:809-13.

title: GAP Score (trauma)
purpose: Simplified version of MGAP using GCS, age, SBP.

references.label: Kondo Y et al. GAP score. Crit Care 2011;15:R191.

title: ABC Score for Massive Transfusion
purpose: Identify trauma patients likely to need massive transfusion.

interpretation.action: Balanced product resuscitation (e.g. 1:1:1) and damage-control approach.

references.label: Nunez TC et al. ABC score for MT. J Trauma 2009;66:346-52.

title: TASH Score (Trauma-Associated Severe Haemorrhage)
purpose: Predict need for massive transfusion in adult trauma.

scoring.notes: Probability of MT computed by logistic regression: p = 1 / (1 + e^(4.9 − 0.3·TASH)).

references.label: Yücel N et al. TASH score. J Trauma 2006;60:1228-36.

title: SAPS II
purpose: Predict in-hospital mortality in ICU patients from 17 physiological and demographic variables.

items.label: Age, HR, SBP, temperature, PaO₂/FiO₂ (if ventilated), urine output, BUN, WBC, K, Na, HCO₃, bilirubin, GCS, chronic disease (metastatic cancer, haematologic malignancy, AIDS), admission type

scoring.notes: Logistic regression. Predicted mortality = e^logit / (1 + e^logit), logit = −7.7631 + 0.0737·SAPSII + 0.9971·ln(SAPSII+1). Use official calculator.

interpretation.meaning: Use for cohort benchmarking, not individual prognostication.

references.label: Le Gall JR et al. SAPS II. JAMA 1993;270:2957-63.

title: SAPS 3
purpose: Predict ICU mortality from data collected within 1 hour of ICU admission.

items.label: 20 variables across three subsets: patient demographics, circumstances of ICU admission, acute physiology in first hour

scoring.notes: Logistic regression with regional customisation equations. Use official SAPS 3 calculator.

interpretation.meaning: Better early-admission calibration than SAPS II.

references.label: Moreno RP et al. SAPS 3. Intensive Care Med 2005;31:1345-55.

title: Logistic Organ Dysfunction System
purpose: Quantify multi-organ dysfunction in ICU.

scoring.notes: Each system contributes 0–5 (or 0–3, 0–1) per published table.

interpretation.meaning: Greater multi-organ dysfunction and ICU mortality (look up via published table).

references.label: Le Gall JR et al. LODS. JAMA 1996;276:802-10.

title: Organ Dysfunctions and Infection (ODIN) Score
purpose: Track sequential organ dysfunction and infection in ICU patients.

scoring.notes: Each item counted only if defined criteria met (see Fagon 1993).

references.label: Fagon JY et al. ODIN. Intensive Care Med 1993;19:137-44.

title: APACHE III
purpose: Predict ICU mortality from 17 acute physiology variables + age + chronic health.

scoring.notes: Use APACHE III equations combined with diagnosis-specific coefficients. Proprietary; widely embedded in commercial ICU systems.

references.label: Knaus WA et al. APACHE III. Chest 1991;100:1619-36.

title: APACHE IV
purpose: Predict ICU mortality and length of stay; current generation APACHE.

items.label: APS variables (as APACHE III), age, chronic health, admission source, prior LOS, emergency surgery, mechanical ventilation, diagnosis category

scoring.notes: Logistic regression with diagnosis-specific coefficients. Use the commercial APACHE IV calculator (Cerner).

references.label: Zimmerman JE et al. APACHE IV. Crit Care Med 2006;34:1297-310.

title: Mortality Probability Model II
purpose: Predict ICU mortality from data at admission (MPM0) and at 24 hours (MPM24).

items.label: 15 variables at admission (MPM0): age, coma, CPR, mechanical ventilation, malignancy, chronic renal insufficiency, cirrhosis, intracranial mass, acute renal failure, cardiac dysrhythmia, cerebrovascular incident, GI bleeding, prior ICU admission, type of admission, infection

scoring.notes: Logistic regression — use published coefficients (Lemeshow 1993). Updated MPM III (2007) is preferred where available.

interpretation.meaning: Calibration recently shown to drift; use locally recalibrated version.

references.label: Lemeshow S et al. MPM II. JAMA 1993;270:2478-86.

title: ACS NSQIP Surgical Risk Calculator
purpose: Predict 30-day surgical morbidity and mortality.

items.label: 21 patient-specific variables (procedure CPT, age, ASA, functional status, emergency, comorbidities), used in a logistic regression

scoring.notes: Use the official ACS-NSQIP online calculator (https://riskcalculator.facs.org).

interpretation.band: Outputs per-complication probability and predicted LOS
interpretation.meaning: Use for informed consent and risk stratification.

references.label: Bilimoria KY et al. ACS NSQIP Surgical Risk Calculator. J Am Coll Surg 2013;217:833-42.

title: POSSUM
purpose: Predict 30-day surgical morbidity and mortality from physiological and operative variables.

items.label: Physiological score (12 variables: age, cardiac, respiratory, ECG, SBP, HR, GCS, Hb, WBC, urea, Na, K)
Operative severity score (6 variables: severity, multiple procedures, blood loss, peritoneal soiling, malignancy, urgency)

scoring.notes: Logistic regression: ln(R/1-R) = −5.91 + 0.16·PS + 0.19·OS for mortality (POSSUM); P-POSSUM uses revised coefficients.

interpretation.band: Output is predicted morbidity and mortality
interpretation.meaning: P-POSSUM is better calibrated for general surgery.

references.label: Copeland GP et al. POSSUM. Br J Surg 1991;78:355-60.

title: P-POSSUM
purpose: Portsmouth-modified POSSUM; corrects overprediction of mortality in low-risk patients.

interpretation.meaning: Better calibrated than original POSSUM for low-risk patients.

references.label: Prytherch DR et al. P-POSSUM. Br J Surg 1998;85:1217-20.

title: ARISCAT Score
purpose: Predict postoperative pulmonary complications after surgery.

interpretation.action: Optimise pre-op, lung-protective intra-op ventilation, escalated post-op monitoring.

references.label: Canet J et al. ARISCAT score. Anesthesiology 2010;113:1338-50.

title: Gupta Postoperative Cardiac Risk
purpose: Predict 30-day perioperative MI or cardiac arrest.

scoring.notes: Logistic regression using NSQIP 2007–08 derivation. Online calculator (https://qxmd.com).

interpretation.band: Output is probability of 30-day perioperative cardiac event
interpretation.meaning: Use alongside RCRI for cardiac risk assessment per ACC/AHA.

references.label: Gupta PK et al. Development and validation of a risk calculator for prediction of cardiac risk after surgery. Circulation 2011;124:381-7.

title: VACS Index (Veterans Aging Cohort Study)
purpose: Predict all-cause mortality in HIV-infected patients on antiretroviral therapy.

scoring.notes: Multivariable point assignment (range 0–164). Use official online calculator (https://vacs.med.yale.edu).

references.label: Justice AC et al. VACS index. J Acquir Immune Defic Syndr 2013;62:149-63.

title: AIMS65 Score
purpose: Predict in-hospital mortality in upper GI bleeding.

references.label: Saltzman JR et al. AIMS65. Gastrointest Endosc 2011;74:1215-24.

title: Forrest Classification (peptic ulcer bleeding)
purpose: Endoscopic classification of bleeding peptic ulcer; predicts rebleeding and mortality.

scoring.notes: Patient assigned to ONE endoscopic class.

interpretation.action: Endoscopic haemostasis; high-dose IV PPI infusion; admit.
Clot removal and treat underlying lesion; PPI.
Oral PPI; early refeed and discharge consider.

references.label: Forrest JA et al. Endoscopy in gastrointestinal bleeding. Lancet 1974;2:394-7.

title: Truelove and Witts Severity Criteria (UC)
purpose: Classify ulcerative colitis flare severity to guide IV vs oral therapy.

scoring.notes: Severe UC = ≥ 6 bloody stools/day PLUS ANY ONE systemic feature.

interpretation.action: Admit; IV corticosteroids (e.g. hydrocortisone 100 mg QDS); VTE prophylaxis; surgical review by day 3 if no response.

references.label: Truelove SC, Witts LJ. Cortisone in ulcerative colitis. BMJ 1955;2:1041-8.

title: Maddrey Discriminant Function
purpose: Identify alcoholic hepatitis severe enough to benefit from corticosteroids.

items.label: DF = 4.6 × (patient PT − control PT in seconds) + total bilirubin (mg/dL)

scoring.notes: PT in seconds, bilirubin in mg/dL. If bilirubin in µmol/L: divide by 17.1.

interpretation.action: Consider prednisolone 40 mg/day (per STOPAH); assess Lille at day 7; treat infection.

references.label: Maddrey WC et al. Discriminant function for prednisolone in alcoholic hepatitis. Gastroenterology 1978;75:193-9.

title: Lille Model
purpose: Predict 6-month mortality in severe alcoholic hepatitis after 7 days of corticosteroids; guides treatment continuation vs cessation.

scoring.notes: Lille = e^(−R) / (1 + e^(−R)) using logistic regression coefficients (Louvet 2007). Online calculator widely available.

interpretation.action: Stop steroids (no survival benefit); consider transplant referral / early liver transplantation per selected centres.

references.label: Louvet A et al. Lille model. Hepatology 2007;45:1348-54.

title: Glasgow Alcoholic Hepatitis Score
purpose: Predict 28- and 84-day mortality in alcoholic hepatitis.

interpretation.action: Supportive care; corticosteroids may not improve outcome.
Likely to benefit from corticosteroids if DF ≥ 32.

references.label: Forrest EH et al. Glasgow Alcoholic Hepatitis Score. Gut 2005;54:1174-9.

title: King's College Criteria for Acute Liver Failure
purpose: Identify patients with acute liver failure who require urgent transplantation.

items.label: Paracetamol — arterial pH < 7.30 (after resuscitation, > 24 h post-ingestion)
Paracetamol — ALL THREE within 24 h: INR > 6.5, creatinine > 300 µmol/L, grade III/IV encephalopathy
Non-paracetamol — ANY THREE of: age < 10 or > 40, non-A non-B hepatitis or drug, jaundice-to-encephalopathy > 7 days, INR > 3.5, bilirubin > 300 µmol/L

scoring.notes: Meeting paracetamol or non-paracetamol limb satisfies criteria for transplant listing.

interpretation.action: Urgent contact with transplant centre; super-urgent listing per UK criteria.

references.label: O'Grady JG et al. King's College criteria. Gastroenterology 1989;97:439-45.

title: MELD-Na
purpose: Predict 3-month mortality in chronic liver disease; used for liver transplant allocation (UNOS since 2016).

scoring.notes: MELD-Na = MELD + 1.32 × (137 − Na) − [0.033 × MELD × (137 − Na)]. Sodium capped 125–137. MELD capped 6–40.

references.label: Kim WR et al. MELD-Na. NEJM 2008;359:1018-26.

title: MELD 3.0
purpose: Updated MELD score (since 2023 UNOS) incorporating sex, albumin and interaction terms to reduce gender disparity in transplant waitlist.

items.label: Variables: bilirubin, INR, creatinine, sodium, albumin, sex

interpretation.meaning: Used for adult liver-transplant allocation (US OPTN policy).

references.label: Kim WR et al. MELD 3.0. Gastroenterology 2021;161:1887-95.

title: iMELD
purpose: Integrate age and sodium with MELD for waitlist mortality prediction.

scoring.notes: iMELD = MELD + (0.3 × age) − (0.7 × Na) + 100.

references.label: Luca A et al. iMELD. Liver Transpl 2007;13:1174-80.

title: BAR Score
purpose: Predict 3-month post-transplant mortality (Balance of Risk).

scoring.notes: Each variable assigned points per published table (Dutkowski 2011).

references.label: Dutkowski P et al. BAR score. Ann Surg 2011;254:745-53.

title: ALBI Score (Albumin-Bilirubin)
purpose: Assess liver function in hepatocellular carcinoma without using subjective variables (ascites, encephalopathy).

scoring.notes: ALBI = (log10 bilirubin × 0.66) + (albumin × −0.085).

references.label: Johnson PJ et al. ALBI grade. J Clin Oncol 2015;33:550-8.

title: Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) Staging
purpose: Stage HCC and link stage to evidence-based treatment.

items.label: A — single or ≤ 3 nodules ≤ 3 cm, PS 0, Child-Pugh A–B
C — portal invasion, N1, M1; PS 1–2
D — End-stage; PS 3–4 or Child-Pugh C

scoring.notes: Patient assigned to ONE BCLC stage based on tumour, performance status, liver function.

references.label: Reig M et al. BCLC strategy 2022 update. J Hepatol 2022;76:681-93.

title: Mayo Risk Score for Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
purpose: Estimate survival in patients with PSC for transplant timing.

items.label: Age, bilirubin, albumin, AST, history of variceal bleeding

scoring.notes: R = 0.03 × age + 0.54 × ln(bili) − 0.84 × albumin + 0.54 × ln(AST) + 1.24 × variceal bleed.

interpretation.meaning: Use for transplant timing and counselling.

references.label: Kim WR et al. Mayo PSC risk score. Mayo Clin Proc 2000;75:688-94.

title: KDIGO AKI Staging
purpose: Stage acute kidney injury severity using creatinine and urine output.

items.label: Stage 1 — sCr ↑ ≥ 0.3 mg/dL within 48 h, OR 1.5–1.9× baseline within 7 d, OR UO < 0.5 mL/kg/h for 6–12 h
Stage 2 — sCr 2.0–2.9× baseline, OR UO < 0.5 mL/kg/h ≥ 12 h
Stage 3 — sCr ≥ 3× baseline, OR sCr ≥ 4.0 mg/dL with acute rise, OR initiation of RRT, OR (children) eGFR < 35 mL/min/1.73 m², OR UO < 0.3 mL/kg/h ≥ 24 h or anuria ≥ 12 h

scoring.notes: Patient assigned to the HIGHEST stage met by either creatinine or urine output.

interpretation.action: Identify cause; review nephrotoxins; optimise haemodynamics.
Nephrology / critical-care referral; consider RRT for refractory acidosis, hyperkalaemia, uraemia, fluid overload.

references.label: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury. Kidney Int Suppl 2012;2:1-138.

title: RIFLE Criteria for AKI
purpose: Classify AKI severity (Risk, Injury, Failure, Loss, ESRD).

items.label: Risk — sCr × 1.5 or UO < 0.5 mL/kg/h × 6 h
Injury — sCr × 2 or UO < 0.5 mL/kg/h × 12 h
Failure — sCr × 3 or sCr ≥ 4 with acute rise, or UO < 0.3 mL/kg/h × 24 h or anuria × 12 h

scoring.notes: Assign to highest stage met.

references.label: Bellomo R et al. ADQI / RIFLE criteria. Crit Care 2004;8:R204-12.

title: AKIN Criteria
purpose: Predecessor to KDIGO; AKI staging within 48 h of insult.

items.label: Stage 1 — sCr ↑ ≥ 0.3 mg/dL or 1.5–2× baseline within 48 h
Stage 3 — sCr > 3× baseline or ≥ 4.0 mg/dL with acute ↑ ≥ 0.5

scoring.notes: KDIGO has largely superseded AKIN.

references.label: Mehta RL et al. AKIN classification. Crit Care 2007;11:R31.

title: Cockcroft–Gault Creatinine Clearance
purpose: Estimate creatinine clearance to guide drug dosing.

items.label: CrCl (mL/min) = (140 − age) × weight (kg) × (0.85 if female) / (72 × serum creatinine mg/dL)

scoring.notes: Use total body weight in non-obese; ideal/adjusted body weight in obese. For SI creatinine (µmol/L): multiply denominator by ~88.4 to convert.

interpretation.band: Result is estimated CrCl in mL/min
interpretation.meaning: Used by many drug-dose references (e.g. DOAC dosing).

references.label: Cockcroft DW, Gault MH. Prediction of creatinine clearance from serum creatinine. Nephron 1976;16:31-41.

title: CKD-EPI 2021 (race-free)
purpose: Estimate GFR for CKD staging without using race coefficient.

items.label: Creatinine-based equation using age, sex and serum creatinine

scoring.notes: eGFR = 142 × min(SCr/κ, 1)^α × max(SCr/κ, 1)^−1.200 × 0.9938^age × (1.012 if female). κ = 0.7 (female) / 0.9 (male); α = −0.241 (female) / −0.302 (male).

references.label: Inker LA et al. CKD-EPI 2021 race-free equation. NEJM 2021;385:1737-49.

title: MDRD eGFR Equation
purpose: Older creatinine-based estimate of GFR (4-variable).

scoring.notes: Now largely replaced by CKD-EPI 2021. Race coefficient removed in 2021.

interpretation.meaning: CKD-EPI 2021 preferred; MDRD still appears in legacy reports.

references.label: Levey AS et al. MDRD. Ann Intern Med 1999;130:461-70.

title: Bedside Schwartz Equation (paeds eGFR)
purpose: Estimate GFR in children using height and serum creatinine.

scoring.notes: For enzymatic creatinine assays. Use updated bedside Schwartz (Schwartz 2009).

interpretation.meaning: Stage paediatric CKD per KDIGO bands; refer nephrology if < 90 with structural disease.

references.label: Schwartz GJ et al. New equations to estimate GFR in children with CKD. J Am Soc Nephrol 2009;20:629-37.

title: Free Water Deficit (hypernatraemia)
purpose: Estimate free-water deficit in hypernatraemic patients to guide fluid replacement.

scoring.notes: TBW = 0.6 × weight (men, children) / 0.5 × weight (women, elderly men) / 0.45 × weight (elderly women). Aim Na correction ≤ 10 mmol/L per 24 h (≤ 8 in chronic hypernatraemia).

interpretation.meaning: Replace gradually with hypotonic fluid (5% dextrose, 0.45% saline) plus ongoing losses.

references.label: Adrogué HJ, Madias NE. Hypernatraemia. NEJM 2000;342:1493-9.

title: Fractional Excretion of Sodium / Urea
purpose: Differentiate pre-renal from intrinsic AKI.

items.label: FENa (%) = (urine Na × plasma creatinine) / (plasma Na × urine creatinine) × 100
FEUrea (%) = (urine urea × plasma creatinine) / (plasma urea × urine creatinine) × 100

scoring.notes: Use FEUrea if patient on diuretics (FENa unreliable).

references.label: Carvounis CP et al. Significance of FEUrea in differential diagnosis of acute renal failure. Kidney Int 2002;62:2223-9.

title: Hyponatraemia Correction Rate Ceiling
purpose: Define safe maximum sodium rise to avoid osmotic demyelination syndrome.

items.label: High-risk patient (chronic hyponatraemia ≥ 48 h or unknown, plus alcoholism / malnutrition / hypokalaemia / liver disease) — max 8 mmol/L per 24 h
Acute (< 48 h) symptomatic — initial 4–6 mmol/L rise to abort symptoms (3% saline 100–150 mL bolus), then slow
General ceiling — ≤ 10 mmol/L per 24 h and ≤ 18 mmol/L per 48 h

scoring.notes: These are SAFETY CEILINGS, not targets. Re-lower (DDAVP / D5W) if overshoot.

interpretation.action: Stop hypertonic, start D5W ± DDAVP (1–4 µg IV) to re-lower.

references.label: Spasovski G et al. European clinical practice guideline on diagnosis and treatment of hyponatraemia. Eur J Endocrinol 2014;170:G1-47.

title: SMART-COP
purpose: Predict need for intensive respiratory or vasopressor support in CAP.

items.label: Oxygen low (age ≤ 50: PaO₂ < 70 mmHg or SpO₂ ≤ 93% or PaO₂/FiO₂ < 333; > 50: PaO₂ < 60 or SpO₂ ≤ 90 or PaO₂/FiO₂ < 250)

references.label: Charles PG et al. SMART-COP. Clin Infect Dis 2008;47:375-84.

title: IDSA/ATS Severe CAP Criteria
purpose: Identify CAP severity meeting ICU admission criteria.

items.label: Major — respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
Minor — hypotension requiring aggressive fluid resuscitation

scoring.notes: Severe CAP = ANY 1 major OR ≥ 3 minor criteria.

references.label: Metlay JP et al. ATS/IDSA CAP guideline. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2019;200:e45-67.

title: Pneumonia Severity Index / PORT
purpose: Risk-stratify CAP for site of care (outpatient vs ward vs ICU).

items.label: 20 variables: demographics, comorbidities, exam findings, labs, CXR

scoring.notes: Step 1: age-based exclusions assign Class I. Step 2: weighted points (age + 10 comorbidities + 5 exam + 7 lab/CXR).

references.label: Fine MJ et al. PSI. NEJM 1997;336:243-50.

title: BAP-65 (COPD exacerbation)
purpose: Predict in-hospital mortality and need for mechanical ventilation in COPD exacerbation.

items.label: Altered mental status (GCS < 14 or new disorientation)

scoring.notes: Combine with age band (< 65 vs ≥ 65) for 5-class stratification.

references.label: Tabak YP et al. BAP-65. Arch Intern Med 2009;169:1595-602.

title: DECAF Score (COPD exacerbation)
purpose: Predict in-hospital mortality in acute COPD exacerbation.

items.label: Dyspnoea (eMRCA 5a if too breathless to leave house but independent / 5b if requires help — score 1 or 2)

references.label: Steer J et al. DECAF score. Thorax 2012;67:970-6.

title: BODE Index (COPD)
purpose: Predict mortality in stable COPD using a multidimensional grading.

references.label: Celli BR et al. BODE index. NEJM 2004;350:1005-12.

title: ARDS Berlin Definition
purpose: Define acute respiratory distress syndrome and severity.

items.label: Timing — within 1 week of known clinical insult or new/worsening respiratory symptoms
Chest imaging — bilateral opacities, not fully explained by effusions, lobar/lung collapse or nodules
Origin of oedema — not fully explained by cardiac failure or fluid overload (objective assessment, e.g. echo)

scoring.notes: All four criteria (timing, imaging, origin, oxygenation) must be met; oxygenation determines severity.

interpretation.action: Low tidal-volume ventilation (≤ 6 mL/kg PBW); prone if PaO₂/FiO₂ < 150; consider ECMO referral.

references.label: ARDS Definition Task Force. Acute respiratory distress syndrome: the Berlin Definition. JAMA 2012;307:2526-33.

title: Murray Lung Injury Score
purpose: Quantify acute lung injury severity; used as ECMO referral criterion.

scoring.notes: MLIS = sum of component scores / 4.

interpretation.action: Consider ECMO referral (e.g. MLIS ≥ 3 is part of CESAR criteria).

references.label: Murray JF et al. An expanded definition of the adult respiratory distress syndrome. Am Rev Respir Dis 1988;138:720-3.

title: LACE Index (readmission risk)
purpose: Predict 30-day readmission or death after hospital discharge.

items.label: Length of stay (< 1 d = 0 to ≥ 14 d = 7)

interpretation.action: Targeted post-discharge follow-up; community care bundle.

references.label: van Walraven C et al. LACE index. CMAJ 2010;182:551-7.

title: Robson Ten-Group Classification System
purpose: WHO-endorsed classification of caesarean section rates for service-level audit.

items.label: 1 — Nullip, single cephalic, ≥ 37 wk, spontaneous labour
2 — Nullip, single cephalic, ≥ 37 wk, induced or pre-labour CS
3 — Multip (no prior CS), single cephalic, ≥ 37 wk, spontaneous
4 — Multip (no prior CS), single cephalic, ≥ 37 wk, induced or pre-labour CS
10 — All single cephalic, ≤ 36 wk (including prior CS)

scoring.notes: Each parturient assigned to ONE group; CS rate analysed per group.

interpretation.meaning: Use for audit. Groups 1, 2, 5 typically drive most variation.

references.label: WHO Statement on Caesarean Section Rates 2015 (Robson classification).

title: Modified Early Obstetric Warning Score
purpose: Detect maternal physiological deterioration peripartum.

scoring.notes: MEOWS varies by trust; commonly a single red (or two yellow) parameter triggers escalation. Use local chart.

interpretation.action: Medical review within 30 min; closer observation.

references.label: CEMACH/MBRRACE-UK confidential enquiries; Singh S et al. Anaesthesia 2012;67:12-8.

title: HELLP Syndrome Severity
purpose: Identify Haemolysis, Elevated Liver enzymes, Low Platelets — severe pre-eclampsia variant.

items.label: Haemolysis — schistocytes, LDH > 600, total bilirubin ≥ 1.2 mg/dL

scoring.notes: All three required for complete HELLP; partial HELLP if subset.

interpretation.action: Stabilise; corticosteroids if < 34 wk; deliver per gestation; transfer to tertiary unit.
Close monitoring; treat as severe pre-eclampsia.

references.label: Sibai BM. Diagnosis, controversies and management of HELLP. Obstet Gynecol 2004;103:981-91.

title: Mississippi Triple-Class HELLP
purpose: Classify HELLP severity by platelet nadir.

scoring.notes: Plus AST/ALT ≥ 70 IU/L and LDH ≥ 600 IU/L.

interpretation.action: Tertiary care; consider delivery regardless of gestation.

references.label: Martin JN Jr et al. Mississippi HELLP classification. Am J Obstet Gynecol 1999;180:1373-84.

title: WHO Maternal Near-Miss Criteria
purpose: Identify women who survived a life-threatening obstetric complication, for audit.

items.label: Cardiovascular dysfunction (shock, cardiac arrest, severe hypoperfusion, severe acidosis)
Renal dysfunction (oliguria not responsive to fluids, dialysis)
Coagulation/haematological (massive transfusion, severe thrombocytopenia, acute thrombocytopenia)
Hepatic dysfunction (jaundice in pre-eclampsia, severe hyperbilirubinaemia)
Neurological dysfunction (prolonged coma, stroke, uncontrolled fits, generalised paralysis)
Uterine dysfunction (hysterectomy due to infection or haemorrhage)

scoring.notes: Any one criterion = maternal near-miss.

interpretation.action: Mandatory audit; learning case for unit.

references.label: WHO. Evaluating the quality of care for severe pregnancy complications: maternal near-miss approach 2011.

title: Fenton Preterm Growth Chart
purpose: Plot weight, length and head circumference of preterm infants against gestational age (22–50 weeks).

items.label: Plot weight / length / head circumference against postmenstrual age on Fenton 2013 sex-specific chart

scoring.notes: Use official Fenton 2013 charts (sex-specific). Track centile changes over time.

interpretation.meaning: < 10th = SGA; > 90th = LGA; falling > 2 major centiles = inadequate growth

references.label: Fenton TR, Kim JH. A systematic review and meta-analysis to revise the Fenton growth chart for preterm infants. BMC Pediatr 2013;13:59.

title: INTERGROWTH-21st Standards
purpose: International standards for fetal and newborn growth.

items.label: Fetal — biometric (BPD, HC, AC, FL) and estimated fetal weight charts
Newborn — birth weight, length, head circumference by sex and gestational age 33–42 wk

scoring.notes: Use official INTERGROWTH-21st calculators and z-score tables (https://intergrowth21.tghn.org).

references.label: Villar J et al. INTERGROWTH-21st newborn size at birth standards. Lancet 2014;384:857-68.

title: Manning Biophysical Profile
purpose: Assess fetal well-being using ultrasound and non-stress test.

items.label: Fetal breathing — ≥ 1 episode of rhythmic breathing ≥ 30 s in 30 min
Gross body movement — ≥ 3 discrete movements in 30 min
Fetal tone — ≥ 1 episode of flexion to extension
Amniotic fluid — single deepest vertical pocket ≥ 2 cm
Non-stress test (NST) — reactive (≥ 2 accelerations ≥ 15 bpm × 15 s in 20 min)

interpretation.action: Repeat within 24 h; consider delivery if term.

references.label: Manning FA et al. Biophysical profile scoring. Am J Obstet Gynecol 1980;136:787-95.

title: Modified Biophysical Profile
purpose: Combine NST + amniotic fluid index as a shorter surveillance test.

scoring.notes: Both must be normal to consider mBPP reassuring.

interpretation.action: Full BPP / CTG / Doppler / consider delivery.

references.label: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 145: Antepartum fetal surveillance.

title: Hadlock Estimated Fetal Weight
purpose: Estimate fetal weight from ultrasound biometry.

scoring.notes: Multiple Hadlock variants exist (1–4 measurements). Built into all modern ultrasound systems.

interpretation.meaning: Compare with population centile (e.g. INTERGROWTH-21st or Hadlock chart) for gestational age.

references.label: Hadlock FP et al. Estimation of fetal weight with the use of head, body, and femur measurements. Am J Obstet Gynecol 1985;151:333-7.

title: ICH Score (intracerebral haemorrhage)
purpose: Predict 30-day mortality after spontaneous intracerebral haemorrhage.

interpretation.action: Beware of self-fulfilling prophecies — guideline guidance not to make early DNAR purely on ICH score.

references.label: Hemphill JC et al. ICH score. Stroke 2001;32:891-7.

title: Hunt and Hess Grading (SAH)
purpose: Grade clinical severity of subarachnoid haemorrhage.

items.label: II — moderate-severe headache, nuchal rigidity, no neuro deficit except CN palsy
III — drowsiness, confusion, mild focal deficit

scoring.notes: Assign single grade. Add +1 for serious systemic disease or severe vasospasm on angiography.

references.label: Hunt WE, Hess RM. Surgical risk as related to time of intervention in the repair of intracranial aneurysms. J Neurosurg 1968;28:14-20.

title: Fisher Grade (SAH on CT)
purpose: Predict cerebral vasospasm after SAH from initial CT.

items.label: 3 — localised SAH > 1 mm or vertical layer > 1 mm

scoring.notes: Modified Fisher (Frontera 2006) is now preferred for vasospasm prediction.

interpretation.action: Daily TCD; nimodipine; vigilance for delayed cerebral ischaemia.

references.label: Fisher CM et al. CT scanning and SAH. Neurosurgery 1980;6:1-9.

title: WFNS Grading System for SAH
purpose: Grade SAH using GCS and motor deficit.

scoring.notes: More objective than Hunt-Hess.

interpretation.action: ICU; consider aggressive aneurysm treatment if survivable.

references.label: Drake CG. Report of World Federation of Neurological Surgeons Committee on SAH grading. J Neurosurg 1988;68:985-6.

title: Hijdra Score (SAH cisternal blood)
purpose: Quantify subarachnoid blood across 10 cisterns and 4 ventricles to refine vasospasm risk.

items.label: 10 basal cisterns — 0 (no blood) to 3 (completely filled) each
4 ventricles — 0 (no blood) to 3 (filled and expanded) each

interpretation.meaning: Greater risk of delayed cerebral ischaemia

references.label: Hijdra A et al. Prediction of delayed ischemia, rebleeding, and outcome after aneurysmal SAH. Stroke 1988;19:1250-6.

title: TICI Grading (post-thrombectomy reperfusion)
purpose: Angiographic grading of reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy for stroke.

scoring.notes: Successful reperfusion defined as ≥ 2b (modified TICI / mTICI).

interpretation.action: Continue stroke unit care; serial NIHSS.
Consider rescue strategies; closer ICU monitoring.

references.label: Higashida RT et al. TICI grading system. Stroke 2003;34:e109-37.

title: ASPECTS (early CT signs in MCA stroke)
purpose: Quantify early ischaemic change on non-contrast CT in MCA stroke; aids thrombectomy decision-making.

items.label: 10-point CT scoring of 10 MCA regions (M1–M6, caudate, lentiform, internal capsule, insular ribbon) — subtract 1 for each region showing early ischaemic change

scoring.notes: Start at 10; subtract for each abnormal region.

interpretation.action: Eligible for thrombectomy within standard time window.

references.label: Barber PA et al. ASPECTS. Lancet 2000;355:1670-4.

title: Modified Rankin Scale
purpose: Measure degree of disability after stroke or other neurological insult.

items.label: 1 — no significant disability, able to carry out usual activities
3 — moderate disability, requires some help, walks unassisted
4 — moderately severe disability, unable to walk without assistance
5 — severe disability, bedridden, incontinent, requires constant care

scoring.notes: Best assessed by structured interview (mRS-9Q).

interpretation.action: Primary endpoint in most stroke trials.

references.label: van Swieten JC et al. Interobserver agreement for the assessment of handicap in stroke patients. Stroke 1988;19:604-7.

title: Barthel Index
purpose: Quantify functional independence in activities of daily living.

references.label: Mahoney FI, Barthel DW. Functional evaluation: the Barthel index. Md State Med J 1965;14:61-5.

title: Functional Independence Measure
purpose: 18-item rehabilitation measure of motor and cognitive function.

items.label: 13 motor items (self-care, sphincter control, transfers, locomotion) — each 1–7

scoring.notes: Higher = more independent. Score 1 = total assistance; 7 = complete independence.

references.label: Keith RA et al. The FIM: a new tool for rehabilitation. Adv Clin Rehabil 1987;1:6-18.

title: Hoehn and Yahr Stage (Parkinson's)
purpose: Stage progression of idiopathic Parkinson's disease.

items.label: 4 — severe disability, can still walk/stand unassisted

scoring.notes: Patient assigned to ONE stage.

interpretation.action: Consider DBS / advanced therapies; multidisciplinary support.

references.label: Hoehn MM, Yahr MD. Parkinsonism: onset, progression and mortality. Neurology 1967;17:427-42.

title: MDS-UPDRS (Movement Disorder Society — Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale)
purpose: Comprehensive 50-item scale assessing Parkinson's disease symptoms and complications.

items.label: Part II — motor experiences of daily living (13 items)

scoring.notes: Each item scored 0 (normal) to 4 (severe). MDS-UPDRS replaces older UPDRS.

interpretation.meaning: More severe PD; subscale changes track treatment response.

references.label: Goetz CG et al. MDS-UPDRS. Mov Disord 2008;23:2129-70.

title: House-Brackmann Facial Nerve Grading
purpose: Grade facial nerve function after Bell's palsy or facial nerve injury.

items.label: II — mild dysfunction (slight weakness on close inspection)
III — moderate dysfunction (obvious but not disfiguring)
IV — moderately severe (disfiguring weakness, incomplete eye closure)

scoring.notes: Used to track recovery; II is most common at 6-month review of Bell's palsy.

references.label: House JW, Brackmann DE. Facial nerve grading system. Otolaryngol Head Neck Surg 1985;93:146-7.

title: MRC Muscle Strength Grading
purpose: Bedside grading of voluntary muscle strength.

scoring.notes: Grade each muscle group bilaterally.

references.label: Medical Research Council. Aids to the examination of the peripheral nervous system. Memorandum no. 45. London: HMSO; 1981.

title: Pediatric Risk of Mortality III
purpose: Predict paediatric ICU mortality from 17 physiological variables in the first 12–24 h.

items.label: Variables: SBP, T, mental status, pupillary reflexes, acidosis, pH, PaCO₂, PaO₂, glucose, K, Cr, urea, WBC, PT/PTT, platelets, age, admission source/diagnosis

scoring.notes: Logistic regression; use published coefficients and the proprietary calculator.

interpretation.meaning: For cohort risk-adjustment; not for individual decision-making.

references.label: Pollack MM et al. PRISM III. Crit Care Med 1996;24:743-52.

title: Paediatric Index of Mortality 3
purpose: Predict PICU mortality using data from first hour of admission.

items.label: 10 variables: SBP, pupillary reactions, FiO₂×100/PaO₂, base excess, mechanical ventilation in first hour, elective admission, recovery from procedure, cardiac bypass, high-risk diagnosis, low-risk diagnosis

scoring.notes: Logistic regression. Use published coefficients (Straney 2013).

references.label: Straney L et al. PIM 3. Pediatr Crit Care Med 2013;14:673-81.

title: Paediatric Observation Priority Score
purpose: Identify children at risk of admission or significant illness in ED.

scoring.notes: Each domain scored 0/1/2 per published rubric.

references.label: Roland D et al. POPS. Emerg Med J 2016;33:864-9.

title: Pediatric Appendicitis Score
purpose: Identify children with abdominal pain who require evaluation for appendicitis.

interpretation.action: Discharge with safety net or observation.

references.label: Samuel M. Pediatric appendicitis score. J Pediatr Surg 2002;37:877-81.

title: Yale Observation Scale
purpose: Identify serious illness in febrile children under 36 months.

scoring.notes: Each item scored 1 (normal), 3 (moderate), 5 (severe).

references.label: McCarthy PL et al. Yale observation scale. Pediatrics 1982;70:802-9.

title: Tanner Staging
purpose: Stage pubertal development.

items.label: Tanner II — onset of pubertal changes

scoring.notes: Separate scales for breasts (girls), genitalia (boys) and pubic hair. Combined with growth chart.

interpretation.band: No Tanner II by 13 y (girls) / 14 y (boys)

references.label: Marshall WA, Tanner JM. Variations in pattern of pubertal changes. Arch Dis Child 1969;44:291-303.

title: Paediatric Glasgow Coma Scale
purpose: Modified GCS for non-verbal / pre-verbal children.

items.label: Eye opening (4) — spontaneous; (3) to speech; (2) to pain; (1) none
Verbal best (5) — coos/babbles; (4) irritable cry; (3) cries to pain; (2) moans to pain; (1) none
Motor best (6) — spontaneous movement; (5) withdraws to touch; (4) withdraws to pain; (3) abnormal flexion; (2) extension; (1) none

scoring.notes: Use age-adjusted verbal scale for pre-verbal children.

references.label: Reilly PL et al. Assessing the conscious level in infants and young children. Childs Nerv Syst 1988;4:30-3.

title: Wood-Downes / HFNC Bronchiolitis Score
purpose: Track severity of acute bronchiolitis to guide escalation to high-flow nasal cannula.

items.label: Wheeze (end-expiratory / inspiratory + expiratory / audible without stethoscope)

scoring.notes: Local variants of the Wood-Downes / TAL / Liverpool bronchiolitis scores exist; use unit's standard.

references.label: Wood DW et al. A clinical scoring system for the diagnosis of respiratory failure. Am J Dis Child 1972;123:227-8.

title: FRAX Fracture Risk
purpose: Estimate 10-year probability of major osteoporotic fracture and hip fracture.

items.label: Age, sex, weight, height, previous fracture, parental hip fracture, current smoking, glucocorticoid use, rheumatoid arthritis, secondary osteoporosis, alcohol ≥ 3 units/day, femoral neck BMD (optional)

scoring.notes: Country-specific algorithms (https://www.sheffield.ac.uk/FRAX). Output is 10-year probability of major and hip fracture.

references.label: Kanis JA et al. FRAX. Osteoporos Int 2008;19:385-97.

title: Garvan Fracture Risk Calculator
purpose: Estimate 5- and 10-year risk of major osteoporotic and hip fracture (Australian cohort).

items.label: Age, sex, prior fractures, falls in last 12 months, weight (and optional BMD)

scoring.notes: Online calculator at https://www.garvan.org.au/bone-fracture-risk.

interpretation.meaning: Use alongside FRAX; differs in including fall history.

references.label: Nguyen ND et al. Development of a nomogram for individualising hip fracture risk. Osteoporos Int 2007;18:1109-17.

title: FINDRISC (Finnish Diabetes Risk Score)
purpose: Screen for 10-year risk of developing type 2 diabetes.

references.label: Lindström J, Tuomilehto J. FINDRISC. Diabetes Care 2003;26:725-31.

title: CANRISK (Canadian Diabetes Risk)
purpose: Adapted FINDRISC for the Canadian multi-ethnic population.

scoring.notes: Use the Public Health Agency of Canada CANRISK calculator (https://www.canrisk.ca).

references.label: Robinson CA et al. CANRISK. Chronic Dis Inj Can 2011;32:19-31.

title: Body Mass Index — WHO / NICE Bands
purpose: Define adult weight categories from BMI.

scoring.notes: BMI categories: WHO standard bands (NICE applies lower thresholds for South Asian and other high-risk groups).

references.label: WHO. Obesity: preventing and managing the global epidemic. WHO Tech Rep Ser 894.

title: Body Surface Area — Mosteller
purpose: Estimate body surface area for drug dosing (commonly chemotherapy).

scoring.notes: Simplest formula; widely used clinically.

interpretation.meaning: Use for chemotherapy and selected drug dosing; cap BSA at ~2.0 m² in some protocols.

references.label: Mosteller RD. Simplified calculation of body-surface area. NEJM 1987;317:1098.

title: Body Surface Area — Du Bois
purpose: Original BSA formula.

scoring.notes: Slightly underestimates BSA in obese patients vs Mosteller.

interpretation.meaning: Historical reference; appears in older protocols.

references.label: DuBois D, DuBois EF. A formula to estimate the approximate surface area. Arch Intern Med 1916;17:863-71.

title: Ideal Body Weight — Devine
purpose: Estimate ideal body weight for medication dosing (e.g. ventilator tidal volume, aminoglycosides).

scoring.notes: Original Devine formula (1974). Used for predicted body weight in ARDSnet ventilation.

interpretation.meaning: Use for tidal volume (6 mL/kg PBW), aminoglycoside dosing; not for actual nutritional weight.

references.label: Devine BJ. Gentamicin therapy. Drug Intell Clin Pharm 1974;8:650-5.

title: Adjusted Body Weight
purpose: Approximate dosing weight for drugs partly distributing into adipose (e.g. aminoglycosides) in obesity.

scoring.notes: Correction factor 0.4 is conventional; some drugs use 0.3 or 0.5.

interpretation.meaning: Use when actual weight > 120% of IBW for selected drugs (aminoglycosides, heparin in some protocols).

references.label: Traynor AM et al. Aminoglycoside dosing weight in obese patients. Antimicrob Agents Chemother 1995;39:545-8.

title: Lean Body Weight (Janmahasatian)
purpose: Estimate lean body mass for pharmacokinetic calculations.

scoring.notes: Janmahasatian formula recommended for propofol, succinylcholine and many other lipophobic drugs.

interpretation.meaning: Use for anaesthetic induction agent dosing in obesity.

references.label: Janmahasatian S et al. Quantification of lean body mass. Clin Pharmacokinet 2005;44:1051-65.

title: Harris-Benedict REE
purpose: Estimate resting energy expenditure (kcal/day).

scoring.notes: Apply activity / stress factor for total energy needs. Mifflin-St Jeor is generally more accurate in healthy adults.

interpretation.meaning: Multiply by 1.2–1.5 (activity / stress) for total daily requirement.

references.label: Roza AM, Shizgal HM. Re-evaluation of the Harris-Benedict equation. Am J Clin Nutr 1984;40:168-82.

title: DKA Severity Classification
purpose: Classify diabetic ketoacidosis severity for treatment intensity and disposition.

scoring.notes: DKA defined by glucose > 11 mmol/L (or known DM), ketonaemia ≥ 3 mmol/L (or ketonuria 2+), pH < 7.30 or HCO₃ < 18.

interpretation.action: Fixed-rate insulin infusion; potassium replacement; treat precipitant.
Aggressive resuscitation; senior endocrine review; cerebral oedema vigilance in young patients.

references.label: ADA Hyperglycemic crises in adult patients with diabetes. Diabetes Care 2009;32:1335-43.
JBDS DKA care pathway 2023.

title: Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale
purpose: Screen for anxiety and depression in physically ill outpatients.

scoring.notes: Sum each subscale 0–21 separately.

interpretation.action: Refer for full mental health assessment.

references.label: Zigmond AS, Snaith RP. The Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale. Acta Psychiatr Scand 1983;67:361-70.

title: Beck Depression Inventory II
purpose: Self-report measure of depression severity in adults.

references.label: Beck AT et al. BDI-II manual. Psychological Corporation 1996.

title: Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale
purpose: Screen for postnatal depression in mothers in the first year after birth.

scoring.notes: Item 10 (suicidal thoughts) requires immediate review regardless of total.

references.label: Cox JL et al. Detection of postnatal depression. Br J Psychiatry 1987;150:782-6.

title: Yale–Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale
purpose: Assess severity of OCD symptoms (obsessions and compulsions).

references.label: Goodman WK et al. Yale–Brown Obsessive Compulsive Scale. Arch Gen Psychiatry 1989;46:1006-11.

title: Columbia Suicide Severity Rating Scale
purpose: Structured assessment of suicidal ideation and behaviour.

items.label: Ideation severity 1–5 (passive thoughts → active intent with plan)
Ideation intensity (frequency, duration, controllability, deterrents, reasons)

scoring.notes: Not a numeric sum — used to classify highest level of ideation and behaviour.

interpretation.action: Psychiatric review; safety plan; consider admission.

references.label: Posner K et al. C-SSRS. Am J Psychiatry 2011;168:1266-77.

title: Montreal Cognitive Assessment
purpose: Brief screen for mild cognitive impairment and dementia.

scoring.notes: Add 1 point if ≤ 12 years of education.

references.label: Nasreddine ZS et al. MoCA. J Am Geriatr Soc 2005;53:695-9.

title: AD8 Dementia Screen
purpose: Brief informant interview to detect dementia.

references.label: Galvin JE et al. AD8 informant interview. Neurology 2005;65:559-64.

title: 6-Item Cognitive Impairment Test
purpose: Brief cognitive screen suitable for primary care.

scoring.notes: Note: higher = more impaired.

references.label: Brooke P, Bullock R. Validation of a 6-item cognitive impairment test. Int J Geriatr Psychiatry 1999;14:936-40.

title: Mini-Cog
purpose: Ultra-brief screen for dementia in primary care and ED.

references.label: Borson S et al. The Mini-Cog. J Am Geriatr Soc 2003;51:1451-4.

title: Confusion Assessment Method
purpose: Diagnose delirium at the bedside.

scoring.notes: Diagnosis: 1 AND 2 AND (3 OR 4) → delirium.

interpretation.action: Identify and treat cause; review medications; environmental optimisation.

references.label: Inouye SK et al. CAM. Ann Intern Med 1990;113:941-8.

title: CAM-ICU
purpose: Detect delirium in non-verbal mechanically ventilated ICU patients.

items.label: 1. Acute change or fluctuation in mental status
2. Inattention (Letters or Pictures attention exam, ≥ 3 errors)
4. Disorganised thinking (≥ 2 errors on 4 simple Y/N questions and a command)

scoring.notes: CAM-ICU positive: 1 AND 2 AND (3 OR 4).

interpretation.action: Re-orient; pain-agitation-delirium bundle; avoid benzodiazepines if possible.

references.label: Ely EW et al. CAM-ICU. JAMA 2001;286:2703-10.

title: Richmond Agitation–Sedation Scale
purpose: Quantify level of sedation and agitation in ICU patients.

scoring.notes: Target typically RASS 0 to −2 in non-paralysed ICU patients.

interpretation.meaning: Target range for most ventilated patients

interpretation.action: Consider lightening unless paralysis/severe ARDS indicates deep sedation.

references.label: Sessler CN et al. RASS. Am J Respir Crit Care Med 2002;166:1338-44.

title: Geriatric Depression Scale (15-item)
purpose: Screen for depression in older adults.

references.label: Sheikh JI, Yesavage JA. Geriatric Depression Scale (GDS): recent evidence and development of a shorter version. Clin Gerontol 1986;5:165-73.

title: Intensive Care Delirium Screening Checklist
purpose: Alternative ICU delirium screen, particularly for patients ineligible for CAM-ICU.

references.label: Bergeron N et al. ICDSC. Intensive Care Med 2001;27:859-64.

title: AUDIT (Alcohol Use Disorders Identification Test, 10-item)
purpose: Screen for hazardous and harmful alcohol use.

references.label: Saunders JB et al. AUDIT. Addiction 1993;88:791-804.

title: CAGE Questionnaire
purpose: Brief screen for alcohol problems.

interpretation.meaning: Clinically significant — sensitive/specific for alcohol misuse

references.label: Ewing JA. Detecting alcoholism: the CAGE questionnaire. JAMA 1984;252:1905-7.

title: Drug Abuse Screening Test-10
purpose: Screen for drug use disorder (non-alcohol).

items.label: 10 yes/no questions about non-medical drug use

references.label: Skinner HA. The Drug Abuse Screening Test. Addict Behav 1982;7:363-71.

title: ASA Physical Status Classification
purpose: Communicate pre-anaesthetic medical co-morbidity.

items.label: ASA III — severe systemic disease (not incapacitating)
ASA IV — severe systemic disease that is a constant threat to life
ASA V — moribund, not expected to survive without operation
ASA VI — declared brain-dead, organs being removed for donation

scoring.notes: Assign single class; subjective — interrater agreement modest.

interpretation.action: Senior anaesthetic and surgical review; consider HDU/ICU post-op.

references.label: ASA Physical Status Classification System (updated 2020).

title: Edmonton Frail Scale
purpose: Multidimensional frailty screen suitable for non-geriatricians.

items.label: General health: hospital admissions in past year (0–2)
Functional performance — Timed Up and Go (0–2)

references.label: Rolfson DB et al. Edmonton Frail Scale. Age Ageing 2006;35:526-9.

title: Clinical Frailty Scale (Rockwood)
purpose: Judgement-based 9-point scale of frailty.

items.label: 4 — living with very mild frailty / vulnerable
