scoring.notes: Based on patient's baseline ~2 weeks before acute illness. Not validated for adults < 65 with stable disability.

references.label: Rockwood K et al. CFS. CMAJ 2005;173:489-95.

title: Visual Analog Scale (Pain)
purpose: Self-report measure of pain intensity on a 100 mm line.

items.label: Patient marks point on 0–100 mm line from 'no pain' to 'worst pain'

scoring.notes: Distance in mm reported; minimum clinically important difference ~13 mm in acute pain.

references.label: Huskisson EC. Measurement of pain. Lancet 1974;2:1127-31.

title: Numeric Rating Scale (Pain)
purpose: 0–10 verbal/written numeric rating of pain intensity.

items.label: Patient selects integer 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst imaginable)

scoring.notes: Minimum clinically important change ~1–2 in acute pain.

interpretation.action: Strong opioid where indicated; review for cause.

references.label: Hjermstad MJ et al. Studies comparing NRS, VRS, and VAS for assessment of pain intensity. J Pain Symptom Manage 2011;41:1073-93.

title: McGill Pain Questionnaire
purpose: Multidimensional self-report of pain quality and intensity using 78 descriptors.

scoring.notes: Pain Rating Index (PRI) = sum of ranked values for chosen descriptors. Short-Form MPQ widely used.

interpretation.action: Use for chronic pain assessment and treatment response.

references.label: Melzack R. The McGill Pain Questionnaire. Pain 1975;1:277-99.

title: FLACC Pain Scale
purpose: Behavioural pain scale for children 2 months – 7 years (or non-verbal patients).

items.label: Face — relaxed (0) / occasional grimace (1) / frequent quivering chin, clenched jaw (2)
Legs — normal (0) / uneasy, restless (1) / kicking, drawn up (2)
Activity — lying quietly (0) / squirming (1) / arched, rigid or jerking (2)
Cry — no cry (0) / moans or whimpers (1) / steady crying, screams (2)
Consolability — content, relaxed (0) / reassured by touch/talk (1) / difficult to console (2)

references.label: Merkel SI et al. The FLACC: a behavioral scale for scoring postoperative pain. Pediatr Nurs 1997;23:293-7.

title: Wong-Baker FACES Pain Scale
purpose: Self-report pain scale for children ≥ 3 years and other patients with limited verbal communication.

references.label: Wong DL, Baker CM. Pain in children: comparison of assessment scales. Pediatr Nurs 1988;14:9-17.

title: Critical-Care Pain Observation Tool
purpose: Behavioural pain assessment for critically ill adults unable to self-report (e.g. mechanically ventilated, sedated).

items.label: Muscle tension on passive flexion (0 relaxed, 1 tense/rigid, 2 very tense or rigid)

interpretation.action: Reassess each shift and after any intervention.
Treat pain (multimodal analgesia per PADIS); reassess within 30 minutes.

references.label: Gélinas C et al. Validation of the critical-care pain observation tool in adult patients. Am J Crit Care 2006;15:420-7.
Devlin JW et al. PADIS guideline. Crit Care Med 2018;46:e825-e873.

title: Behavioral Pain Scale
purpose: Behavioural pain assessment for sedated, mechanically ventilated adults unable to self-report; PADIS-endorsed alternative to CPOT.

items.label: Facial expression (1 relaxed, 2 partially tightened, 3 fully tightened, 4 grimacing)
Upper limbs (1 no movement, 2 partially bent, 3 fully bent with finger flexion, 4 permanently retracted)
Compliance with mechanical ventilation (1 tolerating, 2 coughing but tolerating, 3 fighting ventilator, 4 unable to control ventilation)

references.label: Payen JF et al. Assessing pain in critically ill sedated patients by using a behavioral pain scale. Crit Care Med 2001;29:2258-63.
Devlin JW et al. PADIS guideline. Crit Care Med 2018;46:e825-e873.

title: ABCDEF (A2F) ICU Liberation Bundle
purpose: PADIS implementation bundle to reduce ICU delirium, ventilator days and mortality; track daily compliance per element.

items.label: A — Assess, prevent and manage pain
B — Both spontaneous awakening trial (SAT) and spontaneous breathing trial (SBT)
C — Choice of analgesia and sedation (prefer non-benzodiazepine, light sedation)
D — Delirium: assess, prevent and manage (CAM-ICU or ICDSC)

scoring.notes: Bundle compliance (not a clinical risk score); each element scored 0 (not performed) or 1 (performed) per patient-day.

interpretation.action: Maintain — associated with lower mortality, delirium and ICU readmission.
Identify barriers to missing elements; dose-response benefit demonstrated.

references.label: Devlin JW et al. PADIS guideline. Crit Care Med 2018;46:e825-e873.
Pun BT et al. Caring for critically ill patients with the ABCDEF bundle: results of the ICU Liberation Collaborative. Crit Care Med 2019;47:3-14.

title: Glasgow Coma Scale — Motor subscore
purpose: Standalone motor component of the GCS; performs comparably to total GCS for triage of trauma and ventilated/aphasic ICU patients in whom verbal/eye scoring is unreliable.

interpretation.meaning: Obeys commands — low likelihood of severe brain injury

interpretation.action: Serial reassessment; airway protection if deteriorating.

interpretation.meaning: Abnormal flexion, extension or none — severe impairment
interpretation.action: Equivalent to total GCS ≤8 — secure airway, urgent neuroimaging.

references.label: Healey C et al. Improving the Glasgow Coma Scale score: motor score alone is a better predictor. J Trauma 2003;54:671-8.
Teasdale G, Jennett B. Assessment of coma and impaired consciousness. Lancet 1974;2:81-4.

title: Riker Sedation-Agitation Scale
purpose: Quantify sedation and agitation in adult ICU patients; PADIS-endorsed alternative to RASS.

items.label: 7 — Dangerous agitation (pulling at lines, climbing over rails)
5 — Agitated (anxious, attempts to sit up, calms to verbal instructions)
3 — Sedated (rouses to verbal stimuli, follows simple commands)
2 — Very sedated (rouses to physical stimuli only, does not follow commands)
1 — Unarousable (minimal or no response to noxious stimuli)

interpretation.action: Treat pain/delirium; titrate sedation up only after non-pharmacological measures.
Lighten sedation unless deliberately deep (e.g. status epilepticus, severe ARDS).

references.label: Riker RR, Picard JT, Fraser GL. Prospective evaluation of the Sedation-Agitation Scale for adult critically ill patients. Crit Care Med 1999;27:1325-9.
Devlin JW et al. PADIS guideline. Crit Care Med 2018;46:e825-e873.

title: Pre-operative Functional Status (ACS-NSQIP)
purpose: Single-axis pre-operative ADL classification used in ACS-NSQIP risk models; independent predictor of 30-day morbidity and mortality.

items.label: Independent — performs all ADLs without assistance within 30 days before surgery
Partially dependent — requires help with some ADLs (e.g. bathing, dressing)
Totally dependent — requires assistance with all ADLs

scoring.notes: Classifier only — feeds into the ACS-NSQIP Universal Surgical Risk Calculator and Gupta MICA.

interpretation.action: Consider pre-habilitation, geriatric assessment, multidisciplinary care plan.
Reassess goals of care; explicit shared decision making; ICU/step-down planning.

references.label: Bilimoria KY et al. Development and evaluation of the universal ACS NSQIP surgical risk calculator. J Am Coll Surg 2013;217:833-42.
Scarborough JE et al. Functional dependency and mortality in surgical patients. Ann Surg 2015;261:432-7.

title: Apfel score for postoperative nausea and vomiting
purpose: Predict the risk of postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) in adults receiving inhalational anaesthesia to guide multimodal antiemetic prophylaxis.

items.label: History of PONV or motion sickness

interpretation.action: Two antiemetic interventions of different classes.
Multimodal prophylaxis (≥3 agents); consider TIVA, regional anaesthesia.

references.label: Apfel CC et al. A simplified risk score for predicting postoperative nausea and vomiting. Anesthesiology 1999;91:693-700.
Gan TJ et al. Fourth consensus guidelines for the management of postoperative nausea and vomiting. Anesth Analg 2020;131:411-48.

title: Modified Mallampati classification
purpose: Pre-operative oropharyngeal exam to predict difficult laryngoscopy/intubation; component of multifactorial airway assessment.

items.label: Class I — soft palate, uvula, fauces, pillars visible
Class II — soft palate, uvula, fauces visible
Class III — soft palate and base of uvula visible
Class IV — only hard palate visible

scoring.notes: Assessed with patient sitting, mouth open maximally, tongue protruded, without phonation.

interpretation.meaning: Predicts straightforward laryngoscopy in most patients

interpretation.action: Combine with thyromental distance, neck mobility, mouth opening; plan alternative airway technique.
Awake fibre-optic or video-laryngoscopy plan; senior anaesthetic input; full difficult-airway equipment available.

references.label: Mallampati SR et al. A clinical sign to predict difficult tracheal intubation: a prospective study. Can Anaesth Soc J 1985;32:429-34.
Samsoon GL, Young JR. Difficult tracheal intubation: a retrospective study. Anaesthesia 1987;42:487-90.

title: Wilson Risk Sum for difficult intubation
purpose: Pre-operative composite airway assessment predicting difficult laryngoscopy.

items.label: Jaw movement / mouth opening (0 IG ≥5 cm or SLux >0, 1 IG <5 cm and SLux =0, 2 IG <5 cm and SLux <0)

interpretation.action: Awake fibre-optic or video-laryngoscopy; senior anaesthetic input.

references.label: Wilson ME et al. Predicting difficult intubation. Br J Anaesth 1988;61:211-6.

title: Preoperative Score to Predict Postoperative Mortality
purpose: Estimate in-hospital mortality after non-cardiac surgery using preoperative variables (age, comorbidities, surgery type).

items.label: Age (graded points up to ~9 for the oldest band)
17 weighted comorbidities (e.g. heart failure, chronic respiratory disease, cirrhosis, dementia, metastatic cancer)
Surgery category (weighted by surgical risk; e.g. cardiac, thoracic, aortic, neurosurgery)

scoring.notes: Full coefficient table required for exact scoring; expected in-hospital mortality rises roughly exponentially with score.

interpretation.action: Explicit shared decision-making; consider critical-care booking and senior surgical/anaesthetic review.

references.label: Le Manach Y et al. Preoperative score to predict postoperative mortality (POSPOM). Anesthesiology 2016;124:570-9.

title: Khorana score for cancer-associated VTE
purpose: Predict risk of venous thromboembolism in ambulatory cancer patients starting chemotherapy; informs thromboprophylaxis decisions including pre-operative oncology workup.

items.label: High-risk cancer site (lung, lymphoma, gynaecological, bladder, testicular)
Haemoglobin <100 g/L or use of erythropoiesis-stimulating agents

interpretation.action: Routine education; no routine pharmacological prophylaxis.
Individualised decision; consider prophylaxis in selected patients.
Offer ambulatory thromboprophylaxis (apixaban/rivaroxaban/LMWH) per ASCO/ASH guidance, after bleeding risk assessment.

references.label: Khorana AA et al. Development and validation of a predictive model for chemotherapy-associated thrombosis. Blood 2008;111:4902-7.
Key NS et al. Venous thromboembolism prophylaxis and treatment in patients with cancer: ASCO guideline update. J Clin Oncol 2020;38:496-520.

title: SASM perioperative pathway for known/suspected OSA
purpose: Society for Anesthesia and Sleep Medicine pathway to stratify perioperative risk in patients with known or suspected obstructive sleep apnoea (typically used downstream of STOP-BANG).

items.label: Known OSA on adherent PAP therapy (low add-on risk)
Known/suspected OSA, non-adherent or untreated, but no comorbid cardiopulmonary disease
Known/suspected OSA PLUS uncontrolled comorbidity (HTN/HF/arrhythmia/pulmonary hypertension/hypoventilation/resting hypoxaemia)

scoring.notes: Classifier; combine with surgery invasiveness and anticipated postoperative opioid requirements.

interpretation.action: Continue PAP perioperatively; minimise sedatives; routine post-op monitoring.
Multimodal opioid-sparing analgesia; consider extended PACU stay and continuous SpO₂ monitoring on the ward.

interpretation.meaning: OSA with uncontrolled comorbidity — high risk
interpretation.action: Defer elective surgery for optimisation if possible; otherwise plan monitored bed/HDU postoperatively; senior anaesthetic and sleep-medicine input.

references.label: Chung F et al. Society of Anesthesia and Sleep Medicine guidelines on preoperative screening and assessment of adult patients with obstructive sleep apnea. Anesth Analg 2016;123:452-73.
Memtsoudis SG et al. SASM consensus on intraoperative management of adult OSA. Anesth Analg 2018;127:967-87.
